top_story_title: PAN-OS management-interface RCE (CVE-2026-0322) is on CISA KEV with a 17 October due date
top_story_summary: Palo Alto Networks has published an advisory for CVE-2026-0322, a remote code execution vulnerability in the PAN-OS management interface. The Hacker News reports it carries a CVSS score of 8.6 and is under active exploitation. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 14 October 2026 with a remediation due date of 17 October 2026, describing it as a code injection flaw that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall.
top_actions: Inventory every PAN-OS device and its running version; treat any unit whose management interface is reachable from an untrusted network as priority one.
Check the Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-0322 for the fixed release that matches your train, then upgrade in the change window, HA secondary first.
Until the upgrade lands, restrict the management interface (HTTPS/SSH/API) to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network and remove any internet exposure.
Because the flaw is authenticated and exploitation is confirmed, rotate local admin credentials, API keys, certificates and VPN pre-shared keys after patching.
Review the exported configuration for unexpected admin users, scripts, static routes or modified login pages, and check management-plane logs for admin logins from unfamiliar sources.
executive_summary: CVE-2026-0322, an authenticated RCE in the PAN-OS management interface, is actively exploited and listed on CISA KEV with a 17 October 2026 due date - no fixed release is quoted in the sources, so take it from the vendor advisory.
Three further PAN-OS advisories landed the same day: CVE-2026-0320 (admin command injection, medium) and CVE-2026-0321 / CVE-2026-0317 (denial of service, medium and low).

A suspected advanced actor is exploiting FortiOS path traversal CVE-2025-61624 to deploy PEERSTITCH, a memory-resident ARM64 implant that bypasses checks on tagged VPN sessions; FortiPAM, FortiProxy and FortiSwitchManager share the flaw.
Cisco shipped a Meraki hardening release covering multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities with no workarounds; Cisco states they are not known to be exploited.

F5 and Juniper Networks both patched critical vulnerabilities, with remote code execution and full device takeover reported as possible outcomes - products and fixed versions are not named in the source.
A proxyjacking campaign across 34 countries is hijacking D-Link and Ubiquiti devices to resell victims' bandwidth through a commercial residential proxy network.
Check Point describes Dangerous Deviation Detection, which checks each AI agent tool call before it runs - recorded on the vendor AI defences page.
key_actions: **Palo Alto Networks** — Confirm the running PAN-OS version on every device against the fixed-release table in the Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-0322 - the sources here do not state a fixed build, so do not assume one.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Schedule the upgrade inside the change window, HA pair secondary first, and roll the same change to any device still on an affected train.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Treat this as the same change as CVE-2026-0322 above - one upgrade, not two.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Prioritise devices whose management interface has ever been reachable from the internet, and check their logs back to before the advisory date rather than only from today.

**Fortinet** — Patch FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy and FortiSwitchManager to the vendor's fixed build for CVE-2025-61624 - check the Fortinet advisory for the fixed release, it is not stated in the reporting.
**Fortinet** — Run the vendor integrity checker where one is offered for the platform, and reboot to clear memory-resident code only after capturing volatile evidence if compromise is suspected.
**Cisco** — Read the Cisco advisory to map the CWE-grouped CVEs to the Meraki product lines and firmware trains you run.
**Cisco** — Schedule the firmware upgrade across the estate; stage it - a pilot network first, then distribution, then the rest.

ai_defenses.what_it_does: Checks each AI agent tool call before it runs, rather than screening only what goes into the agent. Check Point's post argues least privilege cannot remove access the agent's job requires and prompt-attack detection does not cover the action the agent is about to take.
